related_questions.question: How do I know which COVID variant I have?
related_questions.snippet: When you receive a COVID-19 test, you won't find out which variant caused your infection. That's because COVID-19 tests only detect the presence of the virus – they don't determine the variant. Genomic sequencing looks at the genetic code of the virus to determine which variant caused the infection.

text_blocks.snippet: Symptoms of COVID-19, including those caused by new variants, can range from mild to severe and may appear 2-14 days after exposure. Common symptoms include fever, cough, fatigue, and loss of taste or smell. Some individuals are also experiencing hoarseness, a symptom that has been reported with a newer variant, XFG.

list.snippet: Fever or chills: A temperature of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher.
Cough: Can be dry or produce mucus.
Fatigue: Feeling unusually tired or weak.
Loss of taste or smell: A change in or loss of the ability to taste or smell.
Sore throat: Pain or irritation in the throat.
Congestion or runny nose: Nasal passages feel blocked or runny.
Muscle aches: Pain or soreness in the muscles.
Nausea or vomiting: Feeling sick to your stomach or throwing up.
Hoarseness: A change in voice quality, making it sound raspy or strained.
Some individuals may experience very mild symptoms, while others may become severely ill.
Symptoms can vary from person to person and may change over time.
If you are experiencing symptoms, especially if you have been exposed to someone with COVID-19, it's recommended to get tested and follow public health guidelines.
